clinicalPearls: Amniotic fluid embolism is a rare, unpredictable, and catastrophic obstetric emergency in which entry of amniotic fluid and fetal material into the maternal circulation triggers sudden cardiorespiratory collapse and coagulopathy
The classic presentation is abrupt hypoxia, hypotension or cardiac arrest, and disseminated intravascular coagulation occurring during labour, delivery, or the immediate postpartum period
Premonitory features may include breathlessness, chest pain, agitation, a sense of impending doom, and altered mental state before collapse
It is a clinical diagnosis of exclusion made on the characteristic sudden presentation; no confirmatory test exists in the acute setting
Management is supportive and immediate: high-quality resuscitation, airway and oxygenation support, circulatory support, and aggressive correction of coagulopathy with blood products
If maternal cardiac arrest occurs undelivered, perimortem caesarean delivery is undertaken promptly to aid maternal resuscitation and salvage the fetus
Because coagulopathy is often severe and early, activation of a massive transfusion protocol and involvement of haematology are key
Risk associations include advanced maternal age, multiparity, placental abnormalities, operative delivery, and induction of labour, though the condition is essentially unpreventable
Care is best delivered by a rapidly assembled multidisciplinary team including obstetrics, anaesthesia, intensive care, and haematology
reference.pathophysiology: Amniotic fluid and fetal cellular debris gain access to the maternal circulation, usually through breaches in the uteroplacental interface or endocervical veins. Rather than simple mechanical embolic obstruction, the syndrome is thought to reflect an abnormal host response resembling anaphylaxis and systemic inflammatory activation. This provokes intense pulmonary vasoconstriction and acute right ventricular failure, causing profound hypoxaemia and cardiovascular collapse, often followed by left ventricular dysfunction. Simultaneous activation of the coagulation cascade produces rapid, severe disseminated intravascular coagulation with consumption of clotting factors and life-threatening haemorrhage.
additionalDifferentials: High neuraxial block or local anaesthetic toxicity
additionalInvestigations: Arterial blood gases to quantify hypoxaemia and acidosis
Full blood count and urgent coagulation studies including fibrinogen to confirm and monitor DIC
Cross-match and activation of a massive transfusion pathway
Electrocardiogram and echocardiography where feasible to assess right and left ventricular function
Continuous haemodynamic and oxygen saturation monitoring
Investigations principally to exclude alternative diagnoses, as no specific confirmatory test exists
redFlags: OBSTETRIC EMERGENCY: sudden peripartum cardiorespiratory collapse or cardiac arrest requiring immediate resuscitation
Rapid-onset severe hypoxia and hypotension during or just after delivery
Disseminated intravascular coagulation with uncontrolled haemorrhage
Maternal cardiac arrest with an undelivered fetus mandating perimortem caesarean delivery
Premonitory breathlessness, agitation, or sense of impending doom preceding collapse
reference.prognosis: Amniotic fluid embolism carries high maternal mortality and a substantial risk of permanent neurological injury among survivors, with outcome strongly dependent on the speed and quality of resuscitation. Perinatal outcome is likewise poor when collapse occurs before delivery. Prompt recognition, immediate resuscitation, perimortem delivery when indicated, and early correction of coagulopathy improve survival, and recent outcomes have improved with organised team-based care.
pitfalls: Delaying resuscitation while seeking a confirmatory test that does not exist
Underestimating the speed and severity of the coagulopathy and transfusing too late
Failing to perform timely perimortem caesarean delivery during maternal arrest
Anchoring on pulmonary embolism or haemorrhage and missing the diagnosis
Not mobilising a full multidisciplinary team early in the event
management: Deliver immediate high-quality resuscitation with early airway control, high-flow oxygen and, if arrest occurs, prompt advanced life support with left-uterine displacement
Support the circulation with fluids, vasopressors and inotropes, avoiding fluid overload given right ventricular failure
Treat right ventricular failure and pulmonary hypertension with pulmonary vasodilators and consider extracorporeal membrane oxygenation in refractory collapse

Correct disseminated intravascular coagulation aggressively with a massive transfusion protocol of red cells, fresh frozen plasma, cryoprecipitate or fibrinogen and platelets, guided by coagulation testing
Undertake perimortem caesarean delivery promptly when maternal cardiac arrest occurs before delivery, to aid resuscitation and salvage the foetus
Control postpartum haemorrhage with uterotonics and surgical measures as needed
Manage in critical care with a multidisciplinary obstetric, anaesthetic, haematology and intensive care team and monitor for neurological injury
